correctness.rationale: For v in part P_i, R(v)=(V\P_i)∪{v}. Every possible input subset either is empty, meets one part, or meets at least two; direct case analysis gives exactly the three boundary pairs and for each nonempty proper A⊊P_i the lower and upper pairs, without duplicates. The coordinatewise inclusion order gives two copies of horizontal sums of Boolean lattices identified at the middle point. This proves cardinality, existence of binary meets/joins, rank/component decomposition and automorphisms; nonmodularity has an explicit violation when factors have sizes ≥3 and ≥2. Distributivity fails for two factors because two complementary proper elements of one factor and one proper element of the other generate M3; the remaining cases are Boolean or a horizontal sum of B2. An independently implemented enumeration verified 134 ordered complete multipartite part profiles on n≤8, exact pair sets, meets/joins, duality, and modularity/distributivity. Finite enumeration is corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The order type, exact cardinality, symmetry group and reverse classification are natural mathematically informative invariants of a nontrivial infinite family of rough-set representations motivated by tolerance rough-set lattice theory. The classification reveals that isolated singleton multipartite parts are invisible to the lattice and distinct B2 components merge into a single symmetric orbit, unlike the higher-rank Boolean components. The modular/distributive thresholds distinguish genuine structural phases. The result is not merely a known existence condition or an unmotivated small-enumeration table.
